items.title: Kent Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 22, 2006
items.q: And during that time as you know, he transcribed a lot of Keith Jarrett’s music, he was very — in terms of influencing me — he was really interested in, at that time, trying to combine sort of like the new thing with the classical thing.

ctx.x: It wasn’t the Pythod, was it? I think that was way back.

It was like — it had a French name. It was just one of those places where we used to go and listen. I used to listen to him because he was like really knowledgeable especially in terms of bop. And during that time as you know, he transcribed a lot of Keith Jarrett’s music, he was very — in terms of influencing me — he was really interested in, at that time, trying to combine sort of like the new thing with the classical thing. And actually on my senior recital he played the Franck Sonata with me, which is an…

handle it. And I saw him for the first time, well I’ve seen him a couple of times, but at the IAJE convention in Long Beach, California about a year and a half ago. And we were talking about how in music you really should concentrate on the instrument first and not really call yourself a jazz musician or a classical musician but really concentrate on the fundamentals because that’s how he was taught. I mean but he was very knowledgeable in terms of jazz, did a lot of transcriptions, did great arrangements, but…
